summary: The candidate routes acceptInvite, leave, and member removal through the same workspace-runtime per-user advisory lock used by the read paths. The new focused test verifies that each read and lifecycle path issues that lock as its first transaction query, and the added comment documents the serialization. No functional defects found.

evidence: src/workspace_outreach_store.ts lines 249, 296, and 339 now acquire workspace-runtime:<userId> for acceptInvite, leave, and updateMember with remove, matching the runtime read paths.
The new comment at src/workspace_outreach_store.ts lines 150-154 documents that provisioning callers and lifecycle operations hold the runtime lock before loading state.

src/workspace_outreach_lock_test.ts lines 21-34 and 71-75 check that workspaceForUser, workspacesForUser, workspaceOverviewForUser, workspaceForUserInTransaction, acceptInvite, leave, and removeMember all issue the workspace-runtime lock first.
The base used workspace-lifecycle-user for those lifecycle operations, so the shared workspace-runtime key is the change that closes the split-lock race.
